chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: The Music Town card, vocal coaching and Spikes's other songs
summary: Austin McCoy did most of the vocal coaching at Music Town; Spikes says he does not sing and has about a hundred songs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You just gave me another card of yours...from Music Town: "Spikes Brothers and McCoy's Music Town -- Music composing, arranging, vocal, recording, dancing, dramatic art, photography -- Benjamin F. 'Reb' Spikes, Lyricist, 1480 West Jefferson Boulevard, Corner Normandie, Los Angeles, California - REpublic 6211" Uh, who was the vocal coach there? I don't remember seeing a vocal...

Oh, we had a [microphone handling noise interference] boy named Johnson was there for awhile but Austin done most of that, you know. He wasn't a singer but he would coach you. You know. He'd play the piano, and if you had a song you wanted to learn, or anything, he'd sing it over with you. He couldn't sing as much as I could but he would coach you, you know [microphone handling noise]...keep you right...keep you singing right.
Me? No. Oho, no, no, no.
Just thought I'd ask. How about the names of some of the other tunes that you wrote? We only have a few names down here, and I know you did a lot of writing.
Oh, I can't think of all those names. I got a hundred songs in there.
And still writing. You're writing religious music now, you told me.
Well, I wrote it for this "Biddy Mason." Yeah. Yeah, I wrote whole gangs down there--ten or twelve songs--for...uh, "Biddy Mason.
